title: Atlantic City
novel:
Marshall and Lily looked at each other across the breakfast table and had the same [[insane|insane]] idea at the same time. "Let's get [[married|marry]]," Lily said. "Now," Marshall added. "Like, right now. Atlantic City. Let's [[elope|elope]]."

They grabbed their [[coats|coat]], jumped on a [[bus|bus]], and headed to the [[casino|casino]] town by the [[ocean|ocean]]. The whole trip felt like a [[dream|dream]] — the [[neon|neon]] lights, the [[tacky|tacky]] [[chapels|chapel]], the old couple who had been married for fifty years and still held hands.

But eloping is not as simple as it sounds. First, they needed a [[license|license]], and the [[courthouse|courthouse]] was closed. Then they discovered that the [[chapel|chapel]] required a [[witness|witness]], and the only person available was a drunk guy named [[Randy|Randy]] who kept calling Lily "[[sweetheart|sweetheart]]."

"This is not how I [[pictured|picture]] my wedding," Lily said, standing in a [[gift shop|gift shop]] buying a [[plastic|plastic]] ring.

"Me neither," Marshall admitted. "But I don't care about the ring or the chapel or the flowers. I just want to be your [[husband|husband]]."

They did get married that weekend — on a [[ferry|ferry]] at [[sunset|sunset]], with the Atlantic Ocean as their [[witness|witness]]. It was [[chaotic|chaos]], it was [[ridiculous|ridiculous]], and it was [[perfectly|perfect]] them.

marry.en: to become someone's husband or wife

elope.en: to run away secretly to get married

coat.en: a piece of warm clothing worn over other clothes

bus.en: a large vehicle that carries many passengers on roads

ocean.en: the very large area of salt water that covers most of the earth

dream.en: things you see and feel while sleeping; a wished-for future

neon.en: brightly colored lights made from a special gas

tacky.en: cheap and of bad quality in a way that looks silly

chapel.en: a small church or a room for weddings

license.en: an official document giving you permission to do something

courthouse.en: a building where legal cases are heard

witness.en: someone who sees an event and can describe it

sweetheart.en: a name you call someone you love; a kind and lovable person

picture.en: to imagine something in your mind

gift shop.en: a small store that sells presents and souvenirs

plastic.en: made from a light, cheap artificial material

husband.en: the man a woman is married to

ferry.en: a boat that carries people and vehicles across water

sunset.en: the time in the evening when the sun goes below the horizon

chaos.en: a state of complete disorder and confusion

ridiculous.en: very silly or unreasonable; making you want to laugh

perfectly.en: in a way that could not be better; completely
